newsitem.title: ITALY: Olivetti PC head sees '96 near breakeven--press.
newsitem.headline: Olivetti PC head sees '96 near breakeven--press.

text.p: Olivetti's personal computer company will be close to breakeven in 1996 and sell more than 800,000 computers, the PC company's managing director Bernard Auer told the weekly economic magazine Il Mondo.

In an interview with the magazine to be published on Saturday, Auer said the mother company accounted for 45 percent of sales from the PC company, while his object was to reduce this to 30 percent by developing its sales network.
Auer said the PC company had a 17 percent share of the Italian PC market but he aimed to boost this to 24 percent.

Olivetti's ex-chief executive Francesco Caio had said earlier this month that Olivetti's PC company would not breakeven in 1996. But the group's new chief executive Roberto Colaninno said last week that he would take a month to assess the company's strategy.
